## How the pieces connect

- A protocol lists only the **minimum** needed to make each buffer (components, final volume, key caveats). Click the buffer's name to open its full page with preparation, storage, reagent details and safety.
- Every buffer page lists the **protocols that use it**, with links back.
- Buffer and protocol IDs (for example `BUF-ACK-LYSIS`, `MUS-LIV-DIG`) are links wherever they appear in the text.
- **PDF:** use the "PDF" link in the right-hand margin of any protocol or buffer page. Links inside a PDF open the published page for the linked document.

## Naming and versioning

Documents are identified by a stable ID, not by their filename:

- **Buffers:** `BUF-<DESCRIPTOR>`, e.g. `BUF-ACK-LYSIS`
- **Protocols:** `<SCOPE>-<SYSTEM>-<DESCRIPTOR>`, e.g. `MUS-LIV-DIG`, `HUM-BLD-PBMC-ISO`, `GEN-FLOW-STD`
- **Files:** `prot_<scope>_<name>.qmd` and `buf_<name>.qmd`

The `version` in each document's header is raised whenever a change could affect results (reagents, timings, volumes); each document ends with a version history. See the [naming guide](protocols_src/templates/naming_guide.qmd) for the full rules.

## Document structure

**Protocols:** Purpose, critical notes, approximate timing, procedure (as numbered steps), protocols used, buffers required, materials, troubleshooting, version history.

**Buffers:** Purpose, linked protocols, working composition, preparation, storage and stability, reagent details, safety, version history.
